newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close mixed, key blue chips rebound.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close mixed, key blue chips rebound.

text.p: Key blue chips rebounded in the afternoon but failed to lift overall market sentiment.
Traders said interest remained keyed on second line stocks of the main board, led by KL Industries which rose further.
"Activities continued to be dominated by second liners," said one institutional salesman. "We still have KLI, Berjaya, Sriwani and Anson as top actives," he added.

Profit taking sales in recent days have dried up, but the market is likely to move sideways in the near term, traders said. The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended up 5.60 points to 1,216.64, after trading as low as 1,207.43.
"Selective buying in core stocks reversed earlier loss in the index," GK Goh Stockbrokers said in its closing commentary.
The blue chip rebound was led by gains in Tenaga, Proton, Tanjung and Sime Darby, which rose between 10 and 30 cents.
But other key blue chips were soft or flat.
Top domestic bank Maybank ended unchanged at 26.00 ringgit after shedding losses in the recent market's slump.
Mohaiyani Securities' banking analyst Amin Manap said some houses had called for downrating of Maybank on fears of competition from other banks, some of which are merging to form larger competitors.
